notes: Landscape handwritten mathematical working sheet, full source 2373 x 1690 pixels. Half a is 1246 x 1690 and half b 1247 x 1690. The two halves overlap at the centre.

The page moves from an Ob/Fl diagram and products to a sequence of inclusions, a product ending in an explicit question, starred pairs and an amalgamation-like construction. Six separate geometric sketches are present. These are descriptions of what is written, not verified mathematics.
The author’s explicit question is the parenthesized (- ?), with a separate point below the question hook. No written title, date or prose doubt occurs.
The F_n relation looks literally like 2, and the F_3 product contains a < shaped wedge. These apparent slips are preserved rather than normalised to equality and multiplication.
The alleged C in the top target and lower replacement has a closed ascending loop. This is reported as a genuine local l/C uncertainty, notwithstanding both witnesses’ C reading.

No consistent inference about intended mathematical alphabets was made. Doubled F is encoded only where separated upright strokes and a white channel are visible. An entry loop or triangular return on an upper arm alone does not force a doubled alphabet.

The top horizontal arrow has a secure live right head and multiple fine/retraced shafts. Its possible older left arrow is not established; literal geometry replaces a speculative deleted relation label.

Overlaid O/F signs are visible at three right-hand positions. Their chronological order cannot be reliably inferred from stroke overlap. The first occurrence carries both orders in place; later occurrences follow its first candidate. The raised mark is peaked at the large occurrences but a compact oblique dot at the subscript occurrence.

Faint reverse-side/show-through material is visible throughout. H calls it a typescript verso, but source inspection did not establish a recoverable sequence of words or a readable front-side typed block. No absent text was reconstructed and no invented illegible-word count was assigned; inventory therefore uses text rather than asserting reused_typed from the editorial note alone.
The solitary 3 at lower left is recorded as an archive sheet number, not a manuscript folio. No cote marker is repeated on this scan.

H_drawing.tex was read in full and its actual coordinates/paths checked against the two source halves. Differences are reported for actual omitted/simplified geometry; the general editorial description is not counted a second time.
No mathematical statement was proved or used as a theorem in this reading; checks is empty. Contextual compatibility only prompted inspection and never supplied missing ink.

No OCR, recognition, web source, other page, other reader output, compilation or subagent was used. Whole, a and b were each viewed once. Eighteen tight crops were each produced and viewed once, with autocontrast and LANCZOS enlargement, no rotation or sharpening.

One text-only comparison of reading.tex with witness C was inspected. The final additional local l/C alternatives were separately added and are explicitly reported in T03 and T09. No source image was reopened for the consistency comparison.

brief_feedback: The explicit authority to inspect H_drawing.tex and the prohibition on treating partial-status editorial notes as local doubts were useful. No necessary instruction was missing. Literal traces are preferable when heavy retracing makes earlier-arrow or overwrite chronology unknowable. The single-view restriction was followed, including the later non-overlapping alphabet crops triggered by uncertainty remaining from the halves.
